name: Dr. Asef Mohammad Redwan
affiliation: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, North South University
biography:
Dr. Asef Mohammad Redwan is an environmental engineering scientist specializing in environmental biotechnology, the biogeochemistry of metal-bacteria interactions, engineered bioremediation of organic and inorganic pollutants, and critical material recovery.

He holds a Ph.D. and M.S. in Environmental Engineering from Texas Tech University (USA) and a B.Sc. in Civil Engineering from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). Prior to founding Waste Mining Lab at North South University, he served as a Staff Scientist and Postdoctoral Researcher at the Idaho National Laboratory (INL) in the United States, directing multiple U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) research initiatives. He maintains an active joint appointment as Affiliate Faculty at Idaho State University and collaborates extensively with ITN-BUET on climate-resilient water and sanitation engineering.
research_interests: Environmental biotechnology; metal-microbe biogeochemistry; rare earth element and critical material recovery; textile wastewater treatment & Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD); AI-driven waste segregation; circular bioeconomy; climate-resilient water and sanitation safety planning.
